And in the year 1595 [of the Greeks = 1199/1200 AD],
528 {OCR? for 595} of the Arabs [= 1198/1199 AD],
al-Malik al-Aziz, son of Salah al-Din, the ruler of Egypt, died.
For he was out hunting,
and when he saw a wolf, he pursued it,
and he fell from his horse and contracted a fever.
And he returned to Cairo,
and died there.
And he left a young son whose name was al-Malik al-Mansur.
Then dissension broke out among the grandees:
for some of them wished to set up the boy in his father's place,
while some of them [preferred] al-Adil,
and some of them al-Afdal.
And the faction of those who wanted al-Afdal prevailed,
and they sent and brought him from Salkhad, and he reigned.
Then those who did not want al-Afdal fled,
and went and took Jerusalem.
And al-Afdal took an army of Egyptians and set out to march against Damascus;
and the Damascenes urgently sent word to inform al-Malik al-Adil while he was warring against Mardin.
He, however, left his son al-Malik al-Kamil Muhammad at the fortress of Mardin,
and went in haste to Damascus.
And al-Afdal also came and encamped against it.
And his forces mutinied against him,
and he abandoned [the siege] and went back to Egypt.
And his arrival was disastrous.
Now al-Kamil, the son of al-Adil, had brought those in the fortress of Mardin into great distress through the lack of provisions and disease that had broken out among them,
and that Nizam al-Din, the regent of the young boy Husam al-Din, was close (to surrendering the fortress?).
When Nur al-Din, ruler of Mosul,
and his cousins,
the ruler of Sinjar and the ruler of Jazira,
heard [of this],
they were perturbed.
And they said to one another:
"If the house of al-Adil gain control over Mardin,
they will take away from us all our territories."
And on this account they eagerly made an alliance,
and they all went to Dunaysir.
And al-Kamil came down from Mardin to the plain,
and the Atabeg's family met him and routed him.
And al-Kamil and those with him fled to Mardin;
and when they went up,
they found that those in the fortress had come down and plundered their tents.
And that very night al-Kamil took his forces and went to Harran,
and from Harran he went to Damascus to his father al-Adil.
